description: Hi! I'm Chi (Aero Engineering, HUST), alongside Son and My Anh (IT & CS, UET). We are utterly captivated by astrophysics, orbital mechanics, and the breathtaking mysteries of the deep cosmos. For this NASA challenge, we aren't just building a project; we are hunting for kindred spirits who share our burning, relentless obsession with space exploration. Let's unite our boundless passion for the universe, combine our technical minds, and build something legendary! 🚀
summary:
We built Terramatch, an interactive web prototype that helps rover teams shortlist Earth analog sites for field testing a Lunar Terrain Vehicle in conditions relevant to the Moon’s South Pole–Aitken Basin.

The prototype maps six candidate sites on an H3 hexagonal grid and ranks them for three test scenarios: crewed traverses, autonomous scouting, and wheel and suspension testing. Using a sample dataset, it shows how terrain slope, ruggedness, geology, surface reflectivity, temperature variation, and horizon obstruction contribute to each score. The ranking penalizes poor matches on criteria critical to each test. Users can also inspect a 10 km elevation profile from Open-Meteo and check for steep segments.

By showing what each site can help test, Terramatch helps teams decide where to focus field surveys and rover trials before a lunar mission. Mars’s Jezero Crater is a proposed target for future expansion.
details:
How do you use it?
Choose a rover test, then click a site on the map. The app shows how the site scored on each factor, how difficult it may be to reach, and which months the team suggests for testing. You can also load a chart showing how the ground rises and falls along a 10 km line. The chart uses 11 elevation points from Open-Meteo and warns you if the steepest 1 km stretch has an average slope above 20°.

What did we consider?
We looked at how steep and uneven the ground is, what kinds of rocks are present, how much light the surface reflects, how much the surface temperature changes, and whether nearby terrain blocks the view toward the horizon. Each test gives more weight to the factors that matter most. For example, rough, rocky ground matters more when testing wheels and suspension. A low score on a factor that matters to the selected test pulls down the overall score.

What is creative about it?
Changing the test can change which site comes first. In our sample data, Askja & Holuhraun ranks first for driving with a crew, while Black Point Basin ranks first for testing how the rover navigates on its own. Users can open both sites and see what drives the difference.

What did we build it with, and who can use it?
We built the website with JavaScript, React, and Vite. We used Leaflet and H3 to show sites in hexagonal map cells, Natural Earth for the basemap, and Recharts for the elevation chart. The rankings use sample data to demonstrate how the tool works. Our goal is to help rover teams narrow down where to visit and decide what to check on the ground before bringing people and equipment to a site.
